title: Product Specification: Condition Monitoring Sensor CMS-200

content.text: Product Specification: Condition Monitoring Sensor CMS-200
Document number PS-CMS200-EN, revision C. Product management: [PERSON_1], [ORG_1]. Technical contact: [PERSON_2], [EMAIL_1].

The CMS-200 is a compact wireless sensor for the condition monitoring of rotating machines such as electric motors, pumps, fans, gearboxes and compressors. The sensor measures vibration and surface temperature directly at the bearing, analyses the signals on the device and transmits condensed condition indicators to a gateway or to a higher-level system. It is designed for machines that are important for production but too numerous or too remote to justify a permanently wired monitoring system.

[ORG_1] developed the CMS-200 as the successor to the wired CMS-100, which has been installed more than 18,000 times since its launch. Customer feedback showed that cabling costs often exceeded the price of the sensor itself, especially in older plants. The CMS-200 therefore combines the proven measurement chain of its predecessor with battery operation, an industrial radio protocol and on-device analytics that keep the amount of transmitted data small.

This specification describes the intended use, technical data, functions, interfaces, installation requirements and ordering options of the sensor. It is intended for product managers, application engineers, sales engineers and the technical departments of customers and system integrators. Firmware-specific details are described in the separate firmware release notes.
The main benefits of the CMS-200 at a glance:
Early detection of bearing damage, imbalance, misalignment and looseness, typically weeks before a failure
Installation in less than ten minutes per measuring point without cabling
Battery life of up to five years with the standard measurement profile
Open interfaces for integration into existing maintenance and control systems
Robust housing for use in harsh industrial environments, including wash-down areas

The sensor is intended exclusively for measuring vibration and surface temperature on stationary industrial machines and for transmitting the derived condition values to a gateway approved by [ORG_1]. It may be used indoors and outdoors within the environmental limits stated in section 4.

The CMS-200 is a monitoring device. It is not a safety component within the meaning of the Machinery Regulation and must not be used to implement safety functions, such as switching off a machine to protect people. Alarms from the sensor support maintenance decisions, but they do not replace the protective devices required for the machine.
Mounting on surfaces with a temperature above 85 °C or on parts that move relative to the machine frame
Use in potentially explosive atmospheres with the standard variant, which is not ATEX-certified
Opening the housing or replacing the battery with a type not approved by [ORG_1]
Operation with a gateway firmware older than version 3.2, which does not support the current radio profile

The CMS-200 is suitable for most rotating machines with speeds between 120 and 12,000 revolutions per minute. The following applications account for the majority of installations at our customers and are supported by preconfigured measurement profiles in the commissioning app.

Centrifugal pumps and fans are the most common use case. They often run around the clock, are spread across the whole site and are only checked during inspection rounds. One sensor on the drive-end bearing of the motor and one on the pump or fan bearing are usually sufficient to detect imbalance, misalignment, cavitation and bearing damage at an early stage. In a typical plant for water treatment or building services, the sensor replaces monthly manual measurements with a hand-held device.

On gearboxes, the sensor detects increasing tooth wear and bearing damage through changes in the acceleration spectrum and the envelope spectrum. Because gear mesh frequencies are often higher than 2 kHz, screw mounting is strongly recommended for this application. For gearboxes with several stages, one sensor per stage gives the clearest diagnosis.

Screw compressors, vacuum pumps and spindle drives of machine tools place high demands on the frequency range and on the measurement interval. For these machines, we recommend the high-resolution measurement profile with a measurement every 15 minutes. With this profile, the battery life of the sensor is reduced to about two years, as shown in section 6.
The following values apply at an ambient temperature of 23 °C unless stated otherwise. Tolerances refer to the delivery condition of the sensor.
2 Hz to 10 kHz (Z axis), 2 Hz to 5 kHz (X, Y)
up to 100 m indoors, 300 m line of sight
standard profile, one measurement per hour
IP69K only with cable gland cover
M8 thread, adhesive pad or magnet

The CMS-200 works in measurement cycles. In each cycle, the sensor wakes up, records the raw signals, calculates condition indicators, compares them with the configured limits and sends the results to the gateway. Between the cycles, the sensor stays in a low-power sleep mode.

The sensor records acceleration in three axes with a configurable measurement time of 0.5 to 4 seconds. From the raw signal, it calculates the root mean square of the vibration velocity in the range from 10 Hz to 1 kHz according to ISO 10816 and ISO 20816, the peak and root mean square of the acceleration, the crest factor and the kurtosis. These values give a reliable picture of the general machine condition and are suitable for trend analysis.

For more detailed diagnostics, the sensor can also calculate an envelope spectrum, which is particularly sensitive to early bearing damage. On request, the complete raw signal of a measurement can be transmitted to the gateway. Because this requires much more energy, raw data transmission should be limited to a few measurements per day, for example once at the start of each shift.

A temperature sensor in the base of the housing measures the surface temperature of the machine at the mounting point. The value is recorded in every measurement cycle and transmitted together with the vibration indicators. A rising temperature together with rising vibration is often the first sign of lubrication problems.

Instead of transmitting raw data continuously, the CMS-200 evaluates the signals on the device. During a learning phase of 7 days after commissioning, the sensor builds a statistical baseline of the normal machine condition for each indicator. After the learning phase, it reports deviations from this baseline in addition to the absolute values.
The analysis uses three condition levels:
: all indicators are within the learned range and below the absolute warning limits.
: at least one indicator exceeds the learned range by more than 50 percent or the absolute warning limit for at least three consecutive cycles.
: at least one indicator exceeds the absolute alarm limit, or the warning condition persists for more than 24 hours with an upward trend.

When the condition changes, the sensor automatically shortens the measurement interval to five minutes for the next two hours so that maintenance staff receive a dense picture of the situation. The absolute limits for warning and alarm can be set per measuring point. By default, the sensor uses the limits for machine group 2 from ISO 20816-3.

The sensor communicates with the gateway through an industrial mesh radio network in the 2.4 GHz band. Each sensor can also forward messages from neighbouring sensors, which increases the range in large halls. All messages are encrypted with AES-128 and authenticated, and the sensor accepts configuration changes only from the gateway it was paired with. A gateway can manage up to 250 sensors.

If the connection to the gateway is lost, the sensor stores up to 2,000 measurement results in its internal memory and transmits them as soon as the connection is restored. Firmware updates are distributed over the air by the gateway and are signed by [ORG_1].

The battery life of the sensor depends mainly on the measurement interval, the measurement time and the amount of raw data that is transmitted. The radio range also has an influence, because a sensor that forwards messages for many neighbours stays awake longer. The gateway makes the data of the sensor available through standard interfaces, so that it can be integrated into existing systems without special software. The following interfaces are supported:
on the gateway, with an information model based on the OPC UA companion specification for condition monitoring
Read access to all indicators, condition levels and battery status
Write access to limits and measurement intervals for authorised users
with JSON payloads, for connection to cloud platforms and the customer's own data platforms
for configuration and for retrieving historical data, documented in the
for direct connection to programmable logic controllers, limited to condition levels and the main indicators
on the gateway for commissioning, diagnostics and local trend displays

For customers who do not want to operate their own software, [ORG_1] offers the hosted condition monitoring portal as an optional service. It provides dashboards, email notifications, a maintenance log and automatic reports. The portal is operated in data centres in Germany, and the data processing is governed by a separate agreement.

Condition monitoring data is not personal data, but it can reveal information about production volumes and machine availability. In addition, a gateway is a network device that must not become an entry point for attacks. The CMS-200 system was therefore developed according to IEC 62443-4-1, and the following security measures are part of the standard delivery:
Each sensor has a unique cryptographic key that is generated during production and cannot be read out.
Pairing between the sensor and the gateway requires physical access to the sensor and the commissioning app.
The gateway supports user roles, strong passwords and certificate-based authentication for OPC UA and MQTT.
All interfaces that are not needed can be switched off in the web interface of the gateway.
Security updates for the gateway are provided for at least eight years after the end of sale.
[ORG_1] publishes security advisories for the CMS product family on its
and handles reported vulnerabilities according to a coordinated disclosure process.

The housing consists of a stainless steel base and a cap made of glass-fibre-reinforced PBT, which is transparent to the radio signal. The base and cap are laser-welded, so the sensor has no seals that can age. A status LED under the cap indicates the operating state during commissioning and is switched off in normal operation to save energy.

The quality of the measurement depends to a large extent on the mounting. The sensor should be installed as close as possible to the bearing, on a flat, rigid surface of the machine housing, with the Z axis pointing radially towards the shaft. Three mounting options are available:
with an M8 stud in a tapped hole. This option gives the best signal quality over the full frequency range and is recommended for all new installations.
with an adapter pad bonded with a two-component epoxy adhesive. The frequency range is limited to about 7 kHz.
with a flat or curved magnet adapter, for temporary measurements and for trials. The frequency range is limited to about 3 kHz, and the results depend on the condition of the surface.
Installation and commissioning are carried out with the commissioning app on a smartphone or tablet. A trained technician needs about ten minutes per measuring point. The recommended procedure is:
Clean the mounting surface and remove paint, rust and grease.
For screw mounting, drill and tap an M8 hole at least 12 mm deep and spot-face the surface.
Mount the sensor with the chosen adapter and tighten it with a torque of 8 Nm.
Activate the sensor by holding the commissioning magnet to the marked point on the cap until the LED flashes green.
Scan the QR code on the sensor with the commissioning app and assign the sensor to a machine and a measuring point.
Check the radio connection to the gateway in the app; the signal quality should be at least 60 percent.
Select the measurement profile and, if required, enter machine-specific limits.
Start the learning phase and document the installation with a photo in the app.

During the learning phase, the machine should run in its usual operating states. If a machine has very different operating states, for example different speeds, separate baselines can be learned for up to four states.

The CMS-200 requires no regular maintenance. We recommend a visual inspection of the sensor and its mounting during the regular machine maintenance, at least once a year. The battery status is transmitted with every measurement, and the gateway reports a warning when the expected remaining battery life falls below 90 days.

The battery may only be replaced by the service of [ORG_1] or by a certified service partner, because the housing must be opened and resealed. Alternatively, the customer can order a replacement sensor at a reduced price under the exchange programme. The expected service life of the sensor electronics is at least ten years.

Every sensor is calibrated at the end of production on a reference shaker against a reference accelerometer that is traceable to national standards. The calibration certificate is stored with the serial number and can be downloaded from the portal at any time. A recalibration is not necessary under normal operating conditions, because the MEMS measuring element shows no relevant drift over its service life. If the sensor has been exposed to a shock above the specified limit, for example because it fell from a height of more than two metres onto a concrete floor, it should be checked by the service before it is used again.

[ORG_1] grants a warranty of 36 months from delivery on the sensor, excluding the battery, which is covered for 24 months. Warranty claims are handled through the service portal. Customers with a service contract receive a replacement sensor within two working days, without waiting for the analysis of the returned device. Our application engineers also support customers with the selection of measuring points, the interpretation of alarms and the integration into existing maintenance processes.
The following table lists the most common messages during operation and the recommended reaction:
No data for more than 3 cycles
check signal quality in the app, check for new obstacles
order replacement sensor or battery service
sensor loose or mounted on a flexible surface
machine not running during the learning phase
restart the learning phase when the machine runs normally
The CMS-200 complies with the following directives and standards:
Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU, including EN 300 328 and EN 301 489
EN 61326-1 for electromagnetic compatibility in industrial environments
UN 38.3 for the transport of the lithium battery

Each sensor is delivered in an individual box made of recycled cardboard. The box contains:
The CMS-200 sensor with the battery installed and in transport mode
An M8 mounting stud, except for adapter-only variants
A printed quick start guide in German and English
A test certificate with the serial number and the results of the final calibration
The commissioning magnet and the commissioning app are not included with single sensors. The app is available free of charge, and the magnet is part of the starter kit or can be ordered separately.
